Roofing Shingle Services & Material Types

Overview of Shingle Roofing Materials: Residential shingle roofs fall into seven distinct material classifications, ranging from cost-effective architectural asphalt shingles ($380–$580/square) to generational natural quarried slate ($1,500–$3,000+/square). Selecting the right shingle system depends on your home's architectural style, local building code mandates, roof slope pitch, and prevailing climate hazards such as hail, hurricane-force wind, or wildfire exposure.

Comprehensive Shingle Material Comparison

Compare the key engineering benchmarks, lifespans, and cost ranges across all seven steep-slope shingle systems:

Material Type Expected Lifespan Installed Cost / Sq Impact Rating Fire Rating Structural Weight
Asphalt 20 to 30 Years $380 – $580 per square Class 3 to Class 4 (UL 2218) Class A (UL 790 standard) 230 – 320 lbs
Wood / Cedar 30 to 45 Years (with maintenance) $750 – $1,250 per square Class 3 (natural resistance) Class A or B (when factory pressure-treated) 250 – 350 lbs
Metal 50 to 70 Years $850 – $1,400 per square Class 4 (Highest UL 2218 rating) Class A (Non-combustible) 140 – 170 lbs (Extremely lightweight)
Rubber 50+ Years $800 – $1,350 per square Class 4 (Superior hail deflection) Class A or C (system dependent) 240 – 310 lbs
Composite 50+ Years $950 – $1,600 per square Class 4 (Highest UL 2218 certification) Class A (UL 790 certified) 200 – 280 lbs
Slate 75 to 100+ Years $1,500 – $3,000 per square Class 3 to 4 (dependent on stone thickness) Class A (Natural non-combustible stone) 800 – 1,500 lbs (Heavy structural load)
Solar 25 to 30 Years (power output warranty) $2,100 – $3,800 per square (before tax credits) Class 3 to 4 (Tempered solar glass) Class A (UL 790 certified) 300 – 420 lbs

Asphalt Shingle Installation

Asphalt shingles are North America's most popular residential roofing system, combining cost-effectiveness, proven Class A fire protection, and rapid installation.

Wood / Cedar

Wood & Cedar Shingle Installation

Natural cedar shingles and hand-split shakes deliver authentic rustic charm, natural insulating R-value, and organic architectural elegance.

Lifespan: 30 to 45 Years (with maintenance) Impact: Class 3 (natural resistance) Fire: Class A or B (when factory pressure-treated)
Wood / Cedar Installation Guide → Cost Breakdown
Metal

Metal Shingle Installation

Engineered stone-coated steel and stamped aluminum shingles combine the traditional aesthetic of slate, tile, or shake with the indestructible strength of metal.

Lifespan: 50 to 70 Years Impact: Class 4 (Highest UL 2218 rating) Fire: Class A (Non-combustible)

Rubber

Rubber Shingle Installation

Engineered from up to 95% recycled automotive tires and virgin polymers, recycled rubber shingles offer near-indestructible impact resistance, eco-sustainability, and authentic slate-shake styling.

Lifespan: 50+ Years Impact: Class 4 (Superior hail deflection) Fire: Class A or C (system dependent)

Composite

Composite Shingle Installation

Engineered from virgin resins and mineral reinforcements, composite synthetic slate and shake shingles deliver luxury aesthetics, Class 4 impact resistance, and a 50-year lifespan without structural reinforcement.

Lifespan: 50+ Years Impact: Class 4 (Highest UL 2218 certification) Fire: Class A (UL 790 certified)

Slate

Slate Shingle Installation

Quarried natural stone slate represents the pinnacle of luxury roofing, offering non-combustible fire protection and unmatched structural durability lasting 75 to over 100 years.

Lifespan: 75 to 100+ Years Impact: Class 3 to 4 (dependent on stone thickness) Fire: Class A (Natural non-combustible stone)

Solar

Solar Shingle Installation

Building-Integrated Photovoltaics (BIPV) seamlessly integrate clean solar energy generation directly into sleek, low-profile shingle tiles without bulky rack-mounted solar panels.

Lifespan: 25 to 30 Years (power output warranty) Impact: Class 3 to 4 (Tempered solar glass) Fire: Class A (UL 790 certified)

Shingle Selection Decision Helper

Best Value & Lowest Initial Investment: Asphalt Shingles

If budget is the primary driver, architectural asphalt shingles provide reliable 20 to 30-year protection, Class A fire safety, and wide color availability with the lowest upfront installation investment.

Best for Severe Hail & High Winds: Stone-Coated Metal or Recycled Rubber

In high-hail storm belts (Texas, Colorado, Oklahoma, Midwest), stone-coated steel and elastomeric recycled rubber shingles carry UL 2218 Class 4 impact ratings that deflect large hailstones and resist 140+ mph winds.

Best for Luxury Aesthetics Without Weight: Composite Synthetic Shingles

If you desire the authentic appearance of hand-split cedar shakes or quarried slate without heavy framing reinforcement or wildfire hazards, engineered composite polymer tiles deliver a 50-year maintenance-free solution.
